blocks.text: Structuring a CFO-Ready Part-Time 20-Hour Custodial Budget

When facility operations managers pitch an in-house part-time 20-hour-per-week custodian to corporate finance, presenting only the hourly wage rate guarantees mid-year budget overruns. A 20-hour weekly schedule equals exactly 1,040 paid hours across a 52-week fiscal year—or 86.67 hours per calendar month using the standard 4.333 weeks/month accounting conversion. Furthermore, even though a 20-hour part-time worker sits below the 30-hour federal Affordable Care Act (ACA) medical benefits threshold, your general ledger still absorbs statutory payroll taxes, janitorial workers' compensation classification premiums, statutory paid sick leave, starter equipment capex, and ongoing paper and chemical consumables.

This capex template part time 20 hr custodian worksheet gives you a copy-and-paste line-item structure calibrated for a benchmark 12,000-to-15,000-square-foot US commercial office cleaned five days per week (four hours per shift, 21.65 shifts per month). Each section contrasts Low/Mid-Market wage bands ($19.00/hr base) against Major Metro Class A wage bands ($23.50/hr base) so you can benchmark the bottom line directly against outsourced contractor proposals ($0.07 to $0.12 per square foot per visit).

blocks.text: Itemizing Line 301 & 401: Starter Equipment Capex and Odor-Control Consumables

New in-house custodial programs often overspend on bulky industrial machines while under-equipping the custodian's daily mobile caddy. On Line 301 (Starter Equipment Capex), your goal is giving a 20-hour employee lightweight, high-mobility tools that cut hallway travel time and fit neatly inside a standard commercial office utility closet.

For daytime or early-evening shifts in Class A executive offices where clients and staff are still on the floor, pairing your primary trash barrel with the Rubbermaid Commercial Brute Rim Caddy Attachment transforms a 44-gallon barrel into a mobile workstation—snapping directly onto the rim with 9 organized compartments and integrated tool clips for spray bottles, wet floor signs, and liner rolls. When the custodian moves into glass-walled conference rooms, reception lobbies, or executive suites, deploying the Rubbermaid Commercial Executive Quick Cart Large provides a stealth-look charcoal caddy with a 60-pound load rating, Teflon-coated fabric protector, and quiet casters that eliminate clattering hallway noise. Finally, under Line 401 (Chemicals & Deodorizers), budgeting for Fresh Products Wave 3D Urinal Deodorizer Screens (10-Box) provides a 30-day enzymatic anti-splash treatment in every men's restroom fixture, preventing the #1 source of executive facility complaints between custodial shifts.

blocks.title: Workers' Compensation Class Code 9014 Separation Rule
blocks.text: Under NCCI insurance underwriting rules in most US states, you cannot classify a dedicated 20-hour in-house custodian under Clerical Office Employees (Class Code 8810, which costs roughly $0.12 to $0.25 per $100 of payroll). Custodial staff must be reported under Janitorial / Building Operation by Contractors or Employers (Class Code 9014 or 9015), which carries a $4.50 to $8.50 rate per $100 of payroll due to slip, lifting, and chemical exposure risks.
How to Compare Your Worksheet Total Against Outsourced Vendor Bids

Once you calculate your Total Monthly Amortized Equivalent on the bottom row of the worksheet ($2,617/month in standard markets to $3,210/month in high-cost metros for a 20-hour/week employee), you must benchmark that number against three outsourced contract tiers before requesting headcount approval:

items: Outsourced 3x/Week Night Service (13.0 visits/mo): For a 12,500 sq ft office at $0.08/sq ft base × 0.95 frequency multiplier ($950/visit base or ~$1,250–$1,650/mo amortized contract with restrooms and breakroom) plus $244/mo in paper consumables, outsourcing 3x/week saves $900 to $1,500 per month compared to a 20-hour W-2 hire.

Outsourced 5x/Week Night Service (21.65 visits/mo): At the 0.90 daily weekday multiplier plus consumables ($2,350 to $3,100/mo total), a turnkey vendor matches or slightly undercuts the loaded cost of a 20-hour in-house custodian while eliminating all PTO backfill, HR turnover, and COI liability from your balance sheet.

Periodic Deep Floor Care Exclusion Check: Remember that a part-time 20-hour custodian equipped with basic hand tools cannot perform quarterly hot-water carpet extraction or VCT rotary stripping ($0.03 to $0.06/sq ft/month). Whether you hire in-house or outsource nightly service, retain a separate $375 to $750 monthly accrual for quarterly specialty floor maintenance.

blocks.text: 5-Step Decision Checklist Before Approving a Part-Time Custodial Requisition

items.name: Step 1: Confirm Daily 4-Hour Workload Against ISSA 3,500 Sq Ft/Hr Standard
items.text: Verify that your cleanable square footage sits between 11,500 and 15,500 sq ft for daily full-scope cleaning (or up to 20,000 sq ft on a zone-rotation schedule) so you neither overpay for idle hours nor set the employee up to fail.

items.name: Step 2: Lock In Written Temp Backfill Pricing
items.text: Contact a local commercial facilities staffing agency to verify their emergency fill-in rate ($40 to $65/hr) and minimum shift hours for the 10 to 14 shifts per year your part-time custodian will miss for sick days, holidays, and vacation.

items.name: Step 3: Audit Closet Storage & OSHA HazCom Readiness
items.text: Ensure your utility closet has lockable chemical storage, secondary GHS bottle labels, an SDS binder, and space to park the janitor's cart and 44-gallon barrel with its rim caddy attached.

items.name: Step 4: Obtain Three Turnkey Outsourced Quotes for Controller Review
items.text: Most CFOs require three competing bids from insured commercial janitorial vendors (including COI verification and consumables line items) alongside your in-house worksheet before signing off on new W-2 headcount.

items.name: Step 5: Assign Weekly Quality Assurance Walk-Through Ownership
items.text: Designate an office manager or facilities coordinator to perform a 15-minute Friday inspection covering restroom enzymatic screens, breakroom microwave/fridge pulls, and HEPA vacuum filter maintenance.

faqs.q: Why does this budget template include 48 hours of temp coverage on Line 204 for a part-time worker?
faqs.a: Even if your company does not offer voluntary paid vacation to 20-hour part-time staff, 18+ US states and numerous cities mandate at least 40 hours per year of accrued Paid Sick Leave, and employees inevitably take unpaid personal days or fall ill. Because a solo part-time custodian has no co-worker on shift to absorb their duties, the facility must either hire a temporary day porter for roughly 12 four-hour shifts per year (48 hours) or let restroom sanitation lapse.

faqs.q: How does turnover affect a part-time 20-hour custodian budget?
faqs.a: Part-time 20-hour custodial positions experience an average annual turnover rate of 35% to 55% because workers frequently leave when offered a full-time 40-hour schedule with healthcare benefits elsewhere. Each turnover event costs $950 to $1,550 in job board advertising, criminal background screening, manager interview hours, onboarding payroll processing, and two weeks of lower productivity.

faqs.q: Can our 20-hour in-house custodian handle interior glass partitions and breakroom appliances within their base budget?
faqs.a: Yes—and that is one area where an in-house budget gains value. Outsourced vendors often bill interior glass and conference partitions as a $15 to $35 per-visit add-on and breakroom/kitchenette appliance sanitation as a $12 to $25 per-visit add-on. With an in-house 20-hour custodian, you can write daily breakroom wipe-downs and twice-weekly conference glass cleaning directly into their 4-hour shift SOP at zero extra surcharge.

faqs.q: What is the cash-flow difference between Year 1 and Year 2 on this custodial budget worksheet?
faqs.a: In Year 1, your cash outlay is $1,320 to $1,760 higher than the amortized budget because you must purchase the starter equipment capex upfront (commercial HEPA backpack vacuum, executive cart, 44-gallon barrel with rim caddy, flat mop system, and microfiber stock totaling $1,980 to $2,640). In Years 2 and 3, capital outlay drops to zero and you only spend $238 to $317/year on replacement vacuum bags, filters, and worn mop pads.
